name: Outschool
line: Outschool's unit is a class the family chooses. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review happen at every problem.
description: AMP vs Outschool: Outschool lists classes by independent teachers. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous, at every problem.
verdict: Outschool's unit is the class: a live video meeting at set times, a self-paced course or a tutoring session, taught by an independent teacher and chosen by the family [1][2][3][4][5]. In AMP, assessment and teaching are continuous. Every answer updates the learner's level and sets the next problem, and each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer.

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after, right or wrong, updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem. In Outschool the family chooses each class, helped by AI class discovery and teacher matching [2][6]. Any grade or assessment is up to the class's teacher and is arranged with the family in advance [2].

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything a learner needs hangs off the problem in front of them: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a video lesson, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. In Outschool the unit is the class. A live class is a video meeting at scheduled times. It may meet once, run for weeks or a semester, or recur each week. Most include independent work before or after the meetings [3]. Across 55 studies, worked examples improve performance in math [9].

reasons.title: Feedback on every answer
reasons.body: After each problem AMP shows whether it was right, the correct answer and the worked steps. In Outschool, feedback is a teacher's. In a live class the teacher meets learners by video at scheduled times [3]. In a self-paced class the teacher gives feedback by message on pre-recorded lessons [4]. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, feedback that explains had the largest average effect [10].

reasons.title: Moving on, and going back
reasons.body: In AMP a skill counts when the learner gets it right without help, more than once. An answer given after a hint or a lesson is marked as helped and does not count as learned. Repeated misses send practice back to what the skill builds on. In Outschool what comes next is the next class the family enrolls in, and Outschool's AI suggests classes and teachers that may fit [2][6]. Certificates of completion are at each teacher's discretion [2].

reasons.title: Continuous review
reasons.body: In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice, at growing intervals, mixed with other math. In Outschool, each class is its own teacher's. Most live classes include independent work before or after the meetings, set by that teacher [3]. We found no scheduled review of earlier skills across classes in the pages we read [2][3]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks, on the researchers' own test [11].

rows.range: Online classes in many subjects, from tap dance to fractions, for ages 1 to 18, taught by independent teachers [1].
rows.start: The family chooses and enrolls in a class, helped by AI class discovery and teacher matching [2][6].
rows.teaching: A teacher on live video at set times, pre-recorded lessons with teacher feedback, or one-on-one tutoring [3][4][5].
rows.next: The family enrolls in the next class. Outschool's AI suggests classes and teachers that may fit [2][6].
rows.mastery: Each teacher decides on any grade or assessment, arranged with the family in advance. Certificates of completion are at the teacher's discretion [2].
rows.review: Most live classes include independent work before or after meetings, set by the class's teacher [3]. No scheduled review found in the pages we read [2][3].
rows.print: None found in the pages we read [2][4].
rows.adult: Chooses and enrolls in each class, and arranges any grade or assessment with the teacher [2].
rows.reports: AI summaries of what a learner experiences in class [6]. No credit for classes; grades or transcripts are arranged with the teacher [2].
rows.evidence: No outcome study found in the pages we read, and no entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse (checked November 2026) [7][8].

theirs: Outschool describes itself as an educational platform of online classes for ages 1 to 18, taught by independent teachers, in subjects from "tap dance to fractions" [1]. Teachers apply to teach, and each class must be approved against Outschool's standards for content, learning goals and teacher expertise before it is listed [2].

A live class is a video meeting at scheduled times. Some meet once, short courses run 2 to 7 weeks, semester courses 8 weeks or more, and recurring classes meet each week. Most include independent work before or after the meetings [3]. Self-paced classes offer pre-recorded lessons with teacher feedback [4], and tutoring is one-on-one, booked from a teacher's available times [5]. The family chooses each class [2]. This page compares Outschool's math classes and tutoring with AMP.
credit: A live teacher who can hear a question and answer it in the moment [3].
One-on-one tutoring with a teacher the family chooses [5].
Each class is reviewed against standards for content, learning goals and teacher expertise before it is listed [2].

theirs: We found no outcome study of Outschool's math classes in the pages we read, and no Outschool entry in Evidence for ESSA or intervention report in the What Works Clearinghouse (checked November 2026) [7][8].

Tutoring in general has strong evidence. Across 263 randomized trials it averaged 0.40 standard deviations, and 0.16 to 0.22 in large U.S. programs measured on standardized tests [12]. That evidence is about tutoring programs, not about Outschool.
ours: Two findings bear on this comparison: feedback that explains had the largest average effect across 40 studies of computer-based feedback [10], and practice that mixes and spaces topics scored 62% against 38% for practice in blocks a month later, in a randomized trial that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations [11]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and AMP is open source.

them: Your child learns best with a live teacher and classmates.
amp: You want assessment, teaching and review in the same practice, with no separate test.
You want a hint, a lesson and the worked answer at every problem.
You want learned skills to keep coming back in practice.
Your child is at different levels in different parts of math.
Your child takes a live class and wants math practice on the days between.

questions.question: How is AMP different from Outschool?
questions.answer: Outschool's unit is the class, taught by an independent teacher and chosen by the family [1][2]. AMP has no separate test: every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does Outschool work?
questions.answer: We found no outcome study of Outschool's math classes in the pages we read, and no Outschool entry in Evidence for ESSA or intervention report in the What Works Clearinghouse (checked November 2026) [7][8]. Tutoring in general has strong evidence in randomized trials [12].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs. AMP places a learner from their first answers, whatever else they use.
